ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Bluewater Foods, Inc. produces packaged seafood, frozen prepared meals and seafood-based snacks sold under the Bluewater, Northern Catch and Tidepool brands. We were incorporated in Maine in 1987. We operate in two reportable segments: Retail, which sells to grocery, club and mass-merchandise stores in the United States and Canada, and Foodservice, which sells to restaurants, cruise lines and institutional caterers.

Our largest customer, a national grocery chain, accounted for approximately 22% of our net sales in fiscal 2024 and 21% in fiscal 2023. Our five largest customers together accounted for approximately 48% of net sales in fiscal 2024.

We source most of our wild-caught pollock and cod from fisheries in Alaska and the North Atlantic under annual supply contracts, and we purchase farmed salmon from suppliers in Norway and Chile. We operate processing plants in Portland, Maine; New Bedford, Massachusetts; and Bellingham, Washington.

As of June 30, 2024, we employed approximately 5,100 people, including approximately 3,900 in our processing plants. Approximately 1,300 of our plant employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, two of which expire in fiscal 2025.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Changes in fishing quotas could limit our raw material supply. Government agencies set annual catch limits for pollock and cod. The total allowable catch for Gulf of Alaska pollock was reduced by 12% for the 2024 season. Further reductions could increase our raw material costs or limit the volume of product we can sell.

Fuel and freight costs are volatile. Diesel fuel for our refrigerated distribution fleet and ocean freight for imported salmon represent significant costs. A 10% increase in fuel prices would have increased our fiscal 2024 cost of sales by approximately $7.4 million.

We rely on a small number of large customers. The loss of our largest customer, or a significant reduction in its purchases, would materially and adversely affect our net sales and results of operations.

Product recalls could harm our reputation. If our products become contaminated or mislabeled, we may need to recall them. A recall could result in significant costs, lost sales and damage to our brands.

ITEM 1B. UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS

None.

ITEM 1C. CYBERSECURITY

Our cybersecurity program is overseen by the Audit Committee and managed by our Vice President of Information Security. In March 2024, a third-party logistics provider that operates two of our cold-storage warehouses experienced a ransomware attack that disrupted its warehouse management system for nine days. We rerouted shipments to other facilities, and the incident did not have a material impact on our results of operations. None of our own systems were compromised.

ITEM 2. PROPERTIES

We own our three processing plants, which together have approximately 640,000 square feet of production space, and we lease our corporate headquarters in Portland, Maine and four regional distribution centers.

ITEM 3. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS

We are involved from time to time in legal proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business. We do not believe any pending proceeding will have a material adverse effect on our financial position.

ITEM 4. MINE SAFETY DISCLOSURES

ITEM 5. MARKET FOR REGISTRANT’S COMMON EQUITY, RELATED STOCKHOLDER MATTERS AND ISSUER PURCHASES OF EQUITY SECURITIES

Our common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol ZZBWF. We paid quarterly cash dividends of $0.21 per share in each quarter of fiscal 2024, compared with $0.19 per share in each quarter of fiscal 2023. We did not repurchase any shares during fiscal 2024.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Fiscal 2024 Overview. Net sales increased 4.3% to $1,842.5 million in fiscal 2024 from $1,766.0 million in fiscal 2023, reflecting price increases in the Retail segment that were partially offset by lower Foodservice volumes. Gross margin was 24.6% compared with 23.1% in fiscal 2023, as lower pollock costs more than offset higher wages. Net income was $71.4 million, or $2.02 per diluted share, compared with $63.9 million, or $1.80 per diluted share, in fiscal 2023.

Liquidity. As of June 30, 2024, we had cash and cash equivalents of $96.1 million and $350.0 million outstanding under our term loan, which bears interest at SOFR plus 2.25% and matures in December 2028. We also have a $200.0 million revolving credit facility, which was undrawn at June 30, 2024. Cash provided by operating activities was $132.7 million in fiscal 2024, and capital expenditures were $58.3 million, primarily for a new freezing line at our New Bedford plant.

Outlook. For fiscal 2025, we expect continued pressure on Foodservice volumes and stable raw material costs. We do not provide quantitative guidance in this report.

ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK

Our term loan bears interest at a variable rate. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in SOFR would increase our annual interest expense by approximately $3.5 million. We purchase some salmon in Norwegian kroner and Chilean pesos; a 10% adverse change in those currencies would have increased fiscal 2024 cost of sales by approximately $4.1 million.
